facts.statement: The genus Hadrosteus was described by Gross in 1932.
Hadrosteus lived during the Frasnian stage of the Late Devonian period.
Fossils of Hadrosteus date from 382.31 to 372.15 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Frasnian to Frasnian (382.31 to 372.15 million years ago)

facts.statement: Hadrosteus was found in the Kellwasserkalk facies of Bad Wildungen, Germany.
facts.quote: Hadrosteus is an extinct monospecific genus of large arthrodire placoderm from the Late Frasnian (Late Devonian) Kellwasserkalk facies of Bad Wildungen, Germany.

facts.statement: Hadrosteus belongs to the clade Aspinothoracidi, which is part of the major clade Pachyosteomorphi.
facts.quote: Hadrosteus is a member of the clade Aspinothoracidi, which belongs to the clade Pachyosteomorphi, one of the two major clades within Eubrachythoraci.

facts.statement: Hadrosteus is classified within the family Hadrosteidae.
Hadrosteus possessed large, double-pronged lower jawbones with serrated edges, indicating it was a fish-eating predator.
facts.quote: It had large, double-pronged inferognathals (lower jawbones), and serrated edges along its mandible, strongly suggesting that it was a fish-eating predator.

facts.statement: The average skull length of Hadrosteus is about 16 centimeters.
facts.quote: The average skull length is about 16 centimeters.

facts.statement: The name of the type species Hadrosteus rapax translates to "Rapacious Strong-Bone".
facts.quote: Etymology The type species Hadrosteus rapax means "Rapacious Strong-Bone".

rejected.statement: Hadrosteus had a triangular snout and a short, high trunkshield featuring a median dorsal plate that was broader than it was wide.
rejected.quote: The head had a triangular snout, and the trunkshield was short, but high, with a median dorsal plate that was broader than wide.
